samples.summary: Image-fetch SSRF guard is check-then-connect: an attacker who controls DNS for a hostname they place in a document's image `src` can rebind between `assertResolvedHostIsPublic` and `fetch`, reaching 169.254.169.254 from the operator's machine.
samples.evidence: `assertResolvedHostIsPublic` (image-fetcher.ts:243-277) resolves `bareHostname(url.hostname)` via `dns.lookup` and refuses non-public answers, then `createImageFetcher` calls `fetchImpl(current, {redirect:'manual'})` (image-fetcher.ts:319) with the *hostname*, so undici performs its own independent resolution. Vector: a workspace member (or an agent-generated doc) writes an image inline `src` of `http://rebind.attacker.tld/x.png`; the attacker serves a 1s-TTL A record that answers `93.184.216.34` for the guard's lookup and `169.254.169.254` for undici's. `wafflebase docs export doc-1 out.pdf` then issues the GET against the cloud instance-metadata endpoint from inside the operator's network. The code comment at image-fetcher.ts:232-235 and docs/design/cli.md acknowledge this, but packages/cli/README.md:39 states without qualification that "A hostname is resolved before it is fetched and refused the same way if it answers with a non-public address" — a guard that reads as covering a named attack is the case nobody re-audits. Exfiltration is limited (the bytes land in the operator's PDF, not the attacker's hands), so this is primarily blind SSRF; closing it needs address pinning below `fetch` (resolve once, dial the vetted IP with a Host header / custom undici connector).

samples.summary: `isPrivateHost` omits several non-public address ranges (multicast, 240/4 + broadcast, 192.0.0.0/24, 198.18/15) and every IPv6 form that embeds an IPv4 address other than ::ffff:, so 6to4/NAT64 spellings of the metadata endpoint pass the guard.
samples.evidence: image-fetcher.ts:84-109 enumerates only 0/8, 10/8, 127/8, 169.254/16, 172.16-31, 192.168/16, 100.64/10 for IPv4 and `::`, `::1`, fc00::/7, fe80::/10 for IPv6, with `unwrapIpv4Mapped` (line 117) folding only the `::ffff:` prefix. Vector: a document `src` of `http://[64:ff9b::a9fe:a9fe]/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/` (NAT64 well-known prefix) or `http://[2002:a9fe:a9fe::]/...` (6to4) is an IP literal, so `assertResolvedHostIsPublic` early-returns at line 257 (`isIpLiteral` is true for anything containing ':'), and `isPrivateHost` returns false because neither hextet pattern matches — the export GETs the metadata endpoint on any host behind a NAT64/6to4 gateway. Same shape for `http://255.255.255.255/` and 224.0.0.0/4 multicast, which reach the local segment rather than the internet. Likelihood depends on the deployment having such a gateway, hence low confidence; impact if reached is the same metadata read the guard exists to stop.

samples.summary: A port-less `WAFFLEBASE_IMAGE_HOSTS` entry exempts every port on a private host from both the literal check and the DNS check, turning the escape hatch into document-driven access to all services on that host.
samples.evidence: `isAllowedHost` (image-fetcher.ts:154-159) matches `h === url.hostname` as well as `h === url.host`, and both `assertFetchableImageUrl` (line 205) and `assertResolvedHostIsPublic` (line 252) return early on a match — no address check, no resolution. An operator who follows README.md:46 and sets `WAFFLEBASE_IMAGE_HOSTS=minio.internal` then lets any image `src` in any document reach `http://minio.internal:6379/`, `:2375` (Docker), `:8500` (Consul) etc. from the export host; response codes/timings distinguish open ports, giving a document author an internal port scanner. The docs (docs/design/cli.md, README) present the portless form as a convenience without noting it widens the exemption to every port. Consider defaulting a port-less entry to the scheme's default port, or documenting the widening explicitly.

samples.summary: `assertNoDotSegments` — the advertised backstop for a call site that forgets `seg()` — only matches the literal `.`/`..` spellings and misses the percent-encoded dot segments WHATWG also resolves (`%2e%2e`, `.%2e`, `%2e.`, `%2e`).
samples.evidence: dry-run.ts:47-51 compares each `/`-split part against the strings `'.'` and `'..'`. The WHATWG URL spec defines a double-dot path segment as `..`, `.%2e`, `%2e.` or `%2e%2e` (ASCII case-insensitive) and resolves all of them, so a future `printDryRun(config, 'DELETE', `/documents/${docId}`)` written without `seg()` and given `docId = '%2e%2e/%2e%2e/workspaces/other-ws/api-keys/k'` would print a URL that normalizes out of the workspace base — exactly the copy-and-run output the guard's own docblock (dry-run.ts:15-18) says it exists to prevent. Not reachable through any current call site (all of them apply `seg()`, and `seg()` escapes the `%`), so this weakens only the backstop. Fix: normalize each segment with `decodeURIComponent`-aware matching, or compare `part.toLowerCase().replace(/%2e/g, '.')`.

samples.summary: Document-controlled image fetches have no timeout and no response-size cap, so an image `src` can hang or OOM an export on the operator's machine.
samples.evidence: `fetchImpl(current, { redirect: 'manual' })` at image-fetcher.ts:319 passes no `AbortSignal`, and `res.blob()` at line 343 buffers the whole body with no length check (no `Content-Length` guard, no streaming cap). An attacker-authored `src` pointing at a slow-loris endpoint stalls `wafflebase docs export` indefinitely; one pointing at a multi-GB body exhausts the process heap. The guard already treats the `src` as untrusted content everywhere else in this file, so the resource dimension belongs with it. Availability rather than confidentiality, hence minor.

samples.summary: `safeEnvelope` spreads arbitrary upstream sibling fields onto the agent's stderr, bounding only length — anything the backend attaches beside `error` is printed unfiltered up to 4 KB.
samples.evidence: formatter.ts:163-170 builds `const whole = { ...body, error }` and prints it whenever `JSON.stringify(whole).length <= 4000`. Only `error.code` and `error.message` are sanitized (`clampUpstreamText` rejects HTML, caps at 500 chars); every other top-level key on an upstream-controlled 4xx/5xx body — a debug context object, an echoed request payload, a header dump — is serialized verbatim into stderr, which for an agent-driven CLI is a channel that gets logged and re-fed to a model. The docblock argues the opposite bound ('a `command` hint is worth keeping'), but the mechanism is a length check, not a field allow-list. An allow-list of known sibling keys would match the stated intent.

samples.summary: The server-supplied `Content-Disposition` filename can still create a dotfile in the caller's CWD (e.g. `.npmrc`, `.env`); `basename` stops traversal but not the name choice.
samples.evidence: `resolveDownloadTarget` (download.ts:25-32) returns `bareFilename(serverName)` — `basename` plus rejection of `''`, `.`, `..`, `-`. A document titled `.npmrc` yields a `Content-Disposition` filename that lands as `./.npmrc` when the user runs `wafflebase files download <id>` with no `--out`. `defaultBinaryIO.writeFile` uses the `'wx'` flag (binary.ts:63) so an existing file is not clobbered without `--force`, which caps this at creating a config file that did not previously exist in the CWD — real but low impact. The docblock at download.ts:10-23 covers traversal but not this case.

verdict.reason: The code is exactly as the finding describes. assertResolvedHostIsPublic (image-fetcher.ts:243-277) resolves the hostname via lookup(host) at line 261 and only throws on a private answer (269-276); it returns nothing and pins no address. createImageFetcher then calls fetchImpl(current, { redirect: 'manual' }) at line 319 with the original hostname-bearing URL, so undici resolves independently at connect time — a genuine check-then-connect TOCTOU, with no pinning anywhere in the package (no undici Agent/connect override, no post-connect revalidation). The path is reachable from attacker-influenceable data: an image inline src flows through resolveImageUrl (310) into guard (311) in the real export commands. The data:/same-origin/allowed-host early returns (250-252) and the IP-literal short-circuit (257) do not cover a public-looking attacker-controlled name, so no existing guard makes this unreachable. The source comment at 232-235 concedes the gap while packages/cli/README.md:39-41 claims resolution-based protection without qualification. SSRF is explicitly in the Security lens lane and severity is impact-based (blind SSRF to cloud instance metadata from the operator's network), so no refutation ground (not-present, already-guarded, out-of-scope) applies.

verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as claimed. isPrivateHost (image-fetcher.ts:84-109) covers only 0/8, 10/8, 127/8, 169.254/16, 172.16-31, 192.168/16, 100.64/10 and ::, ::1, fc00::/7, fe80::/10 — nothing for 224/4 multicast, 240/4 + 255.255.255.255, 192.0.0.0/24, or 198.18/15. unwrapIpv4Mapped (117-127) folds only the ::ffff: prefix in its two regexes (118, 121), so NAT64 (64:ff9b::a9fe:a9fe) and 6to4 (2002:a9fe:a9fe::) spellings of 169.254.169.254 match no branch and isPrivateHost returns false at line 108. assertResolvedHostIsPublic then early-returns at line 257 because isIpLiteral (130-132) is true for any host containing ':', so no second check occurs. I traced the full reachable path: createImageFetcher's guard (299-307) -> assertFetchableImageUrl passes scheme (198), origin (204), allow-list (205), and isPrivateHost (206) -> fetchImpl at 319 issues the GET; the same guard on redirect targets (356) does not help. isPrivateHost is called only at 206 and 269, so there is no other classifier or caller-side guard that closes the gap. This is an incomplete SSRF address guard, squarely in the security lane, and the metadata-endpoint read is the exact harm the guard exists to prevent. No refutation ground applies.

finding.summary: SSRF guard only inspects IP literals, so a public DNS name that resolves to the metadata endpoint (e.g. `169.254.169.254.nip.io`) is fetched — defeating the protection the README/design doc advertise
finding.evidence:
`assertFetchableImageUrl` ends with `if (isPrivateHost(url.hostname)) throw` (image-fetcher.ts:186). `isPrivateHost` only matches loopback *names* (`localhost`, `*.localhost`) and IP *literals* (image-fetcher.ts:74-102); any other hostname falls through and is fetched.

Attack chain, fully traced: (1) an attacker who can write document content — another workspace member, a shared doc, or an agent generating content — sets an image inline `src` to `http://169.254.169.254.nip.io/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/<role>` (nip.io/sslip.io are public wildcard DNS that resolve the embedded literal; `metadata.google.internal` and bare single-label intranet names work the same way). (2) The victim runs `wafflebase docs export <id> out.docx` (packages/cli/src/commands/docs.ts:261) or `slides export` (commands/slides.ts:209), which builds the fetcher and passes it into `DocxExporter.export` / `PdfExporter.export`. (3) `resolveImageUrl` passes the absolute URL through unchanged; `assertFetchableImageUrl` sees hostname `169.254.169.254.nip.io`, which is not in `LOOPBACK_HOSTS`, does not end in `.localhost`, and does not match the IPv4 or IPv6 literal regexes — so no throw. (4) `fetchImpl(current, {redirect:'manual'})` (image-fetcher.ts:221) issues the GET from the operator's machine, and `res.blob()` (line 232) hands the response body to the exporter, which streams it verbatim into the DOCX zip / PDF image stream. The credentials therefore land in the exported file the attacker can later request.

The code comment at image-fetcher.ts:160-162 acknowledges this as a limitation, but README.md and docs/design/cli.md §10 both present the guard as the thing that stops an image `src` aiming an export at `169.254.169.254`, and the refusal message even names the escape hatch — so operators will read this as covered. A guard that reads as covering the named attack while a one-token DNS trick walks around it is worse than none. Closing it needs DNS resolution plus connect-time add

verdict.reason: The claimed gap is not present. The SSRF guard is not URL-string-only: `createImageFetcher`'s `guard` (image-fetcher.ts:299-307) calls `assertFetchableImageUrl` AND `assertResolvedHostIsPublic` (:243-277), the latter resolving the hostname through the OS resolver (`defaultLookup`, :215-218 — the same `getaddrinfo` fetch dials) and throwing if any returned address is private (:269-276). The finding's exact example, `169.254.169.254.nip.io`, resolves to `169.254.169.254`, matched by isPrivateHost at :98, so it is refused before any request. The guard runs before the first fetch (:311) and again on every redirect target (:356), with `redirect: 'manual'` (:319) preventing unchecked hops; unresolvable names fail closed (:262-267). Production call sites (commands/docs.ts:261-263, commands/slides.ts:209) pass no `lookup` override, so the real resolver is used. Tests at test/image-fetcher.test.ts:564-573 and :493-496 pin this behaviour. The line numbers and the quoted "acknowledged limitation" comment in the finding do not match the file's contents (:160-162 is the isAllowedHost doc comment; the URL-literal throw is :206-211). Residual DNS-rebinding TOCTOU is acknowledged at :232-235 but is a different, far harder attack than the reported one-token DNS bypass.
